title: Phishing guidance
summary: Fraudulent links, unsolicited messages and lookalike websites can be used to steal banking credentials.
source_name: Bank Negara Malaysia — Financial Fraud Alerts

title: Mobile application scam guidance
summary: Suspicious third-party applications can expose transaction alerts, OTPs and device access.
source_name: Bank Negara Malaysia — Financial Fraud Alerts

title: Mule account guidance
summary: Accounts offered for rent or used to receive and transfer suspicious funds can expose users to financial and legal harm.

title: Financial Consumer Alert List
summary: BNM maintains an alert list for entities or schemes that may be wrongly represented as licensed or regulated by BNM.
source_name: Bank Negara Malaysia — Financial Consumer Alert List

title: Financial Consumer Alert update — 3 August 2026
summary: BNM added multiple unauthorised entities and potential clone entities to its Financial Consumer Alert list on 3 August 2026.
source_name: Bank Negara Malaysia — Financial Consumer Alert update

title: Alert on fake websites and messages impersonating BNM
summary: BNM warns that messages and fake websites using its name may request identity or banking credentials and should not be trusted.
source_name: Bank Negara Malaysia — Fraud and Scam Notices

title: What to do after a financial scam
summary: BNM advises scam victims to immediately contact their bank or NSRC 997 and lodge a police report. This is response guidance, not evidence that a scanned item is fraudulent.
source_name: Bank Negara Malaysia — Financial Scams FAQ

title: Scam Alert
summary: PDRM publishes scam alerts and advises the public to verify suspicious account, phone and payment details through official channels.

title: Scammers impersonating BNM and demanding a security deposit
summary: PDRM warned about scammers impersonating Bank Negara Malaysia officers and asking victims to pay a so-called security deposit before receiving money. PDRM advises victims not to pay, to stop communication, verify suspicious accounts or phone numbers through Semak Mule, and contact NSRC 997 if victimised.
